diagrams.title: Oral Ulcer and Erosion Differential
diagrams.subtitle: A morphology-first pathway from common aphthae to systemic and scarring disease

steps.prompt: Is the lesion a discrete punched-out ulcer, or a broad erosion/desquamative gingivitis/blister?
Is it solitary and persistent >2–3 weeks, indurated/fixed, unexplained bleeding, or associated with adenopathy?
Prompt biopsy for malignancy and other persistent-ulcer causes
steps.detail: Sample the edge and base for H&E; add cultures or special studies according to host and morphology.

steps.prompt: Recurrent round/oval painful ulcers on nonkeratinized mucosa with complete healing?

steps.detail: Clinical diagnosis; topical anti-inflammatory and analgesic care. Investigate secondary causes only when onset, severity, systemic symptoms, or examination is atypical.

steps.prompt: Genital ulcers/scars, uveitis, vascular/neurologic disease, papulopustules, or pathergy?

steps.detail: Document recurrence and organ domains; urgent ophthalmology for eye symptoms. Classification criteria support but do not replace clinical diagnosis.
CBC/differential, iron/B12/folate, celiac/IBD, HIV/immunodeficiency, medication/toxin, cyclic neutropenia, and autoinflammatory causes according to phenotype.

steps.prompt: Fresh grouped vesicles/erosions on keratinized mucosa or immunocompromised host?

steps.detail: HSV PCR from fresh lesion; consider CMV, syphilis, fungal/mycobacterial disease and culture/biopsy according to host.

steps.prompt: Broaden to IBD, lupus, reactive arthritis, drug injury, hematologic disease, trauma, and malignancy
steps.detail: Use systemic clues and biopsy if persistent or diagnostically uncertain.

steps.prompt: Are there fragile bullae, desquamative gingivitis, chronic widespread erosions, or ocular/genital scarring symptoms?

steps.detail: Lesional/perilesional edge for H&E in formalin plus perilesional or normal-appearing mucosa for DIF in correct medium; add BP180/BP230, desmoglein, laminin-332, type VII collagen or other serology according to phenotype.

steps.prompt: Consider erosive lichen planus, lupus, erythema multiforme, contact/drug reaction, trauma, infection, and nutritional disease
steps.detail: Biopsy persistent or unclear disease; correlate with skin, eye, genital, and medication findings.

diagrams.title: Oral Biopsy and Direct Immunofluorescence Workflow
diagrams.subtitle: Use separate specimens, correct sites, and correct transport media

items.label: Map exact site and keratinization
items.detail: Buccal/labial mucosa, tongue, floor of mouth, soft palate, hard palate, attached gingiva and vermilion have different differentials.

items.label: Look for primary vesicle/bulla, desquamative gingivitis, reticulation, induration, necrosis, or scar
Examine skin, eyes, nose, genital/perianal mucosa and nails
Persistent ulcer
items.detail: Biopsy the active edge including adjacent epithelium and adequate lamina propria; avoid only necrotic center.

items.label: Suspected autoimmune blistering
items.detail: Biopsy the edge of a fresh blister/erosion for routine histology.

items.label: Suspected malignancy
items.detail: Ensure sufficient depth; coordinate incisional/excisional approach with oral surgery/ENT when needed.

items.label: Take a separate specimen from perilesional or normal-appearing mucosa
items.detail: Normal buccal mucosa can have high diagnostic yield in pemphigus/MMP and may be easier than friable perilesional tissue.

items.label: Place in Michel’s/Zeus medium or laboratory-approved transport; never formalin.
State the differential
items.detail: Pemphigus, MMP, linear IgA disease, EBA, lupus, or lichen planus patterns require different interpretation.

items.label: Fresh vesicle/ulcer swab for HSV PCR when indicated
Deep tissue culture for atypical infection in immunocompromised or persistent lesions
Do not let nonspecific surface colonization substitute for tissue diagnosis
